previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A postpartum patient with a history of pre-eclampsia, bipolar disorder, hypothyroidism, and asthma was readmitted on postpartum day 7 for severe-range hypertension and persistent headache. She had been discharged two days prior with stable blood pressures but developed systolic pressures in the 160–180 range at home. In the hospital, she received IV labetalol and started on nifedipine, with excellent response and stabilization of blood pressure. Labs ruled out HELLP syndrome, and proteinuria was mild. Her headache improved with blood pressure control and analgesics. She remained mentally stable on quetiapine, and her ECT session was postponed. She was discharged home on day 2 with nifedipine, continued psychiatric and thyroid medications, and a follow-up plan. Acyclovir was added for viral prophylaxis given postpartum vulnerability.
problems: Endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases complicating the puerperium
